title: Strict hot spots on simply connected planar domains
description: On a bounded simply connected planar domain with smooth boundary, no eigenfunction of the first positive Neumann eigenvalue has an interior critical point, so its maximum and minimum are attained only on the boundary: Burdzy's simply connected hot-spots conjecture, in strict form and for every eigenfunction. The proof: Filonov's gap between the Neumann and Dirichlet eigenvalues; a conformal map smooth up to the boundary, boundary signs and the multiplicity bound; Rohleder's variational principle for tangent vector fields; boundary kernels of the disc with a subcritical potential and a multiplier identity; conditional negativity of a reciprocal kernel through matrices with one positive eigenvalue; a Hilbert-space embedding of the circle. Standard facts on Sobolev spaces and elliptic regularity are named hypotheses. The course is an exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026).
